themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 586% increase (z-score: 6.57)—suggesting either a sudden dumping problem or a breakdown in bike-share maintenance in Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights.
evidence: 6 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (586% spike)
Z-score of 6.57 indicates statistically rare event
Last week also saw 6 complaints, suggesting sustained acceleration
reporting_angles: Are Citi Bike or other bike-share operators failing to retrieve abandoned inventory in this district?
Is illegal bike dumping emerging as a new disposal problem in Bay Ridge?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints reached 12 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 5.2 per week—a 129% spike (z-score: 5.63)—indicating a potential coordination of waste disposal or organized dumping activity in the district.
evidence: 12 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (129% increase)
Z-score of 5.63 indicates statistically significant deviation
Community board has standing request for 'other garbage collection and recycling infrastructure requests' suggesting chronic capacity problem
reporting_angles: Are specific sites or corridors becoming dumping hotspots? Map the complaints.
Is this tied to construction activity (451 DOB filings in 90 days) generating debris?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampment Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.6 per week—a 515% spike (z-score: 4.49)—and the community board has filed repeated requests for homeless services, suggesting a visible crisis that elected officials are aware of but struggling to address.
evidence: 10 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (515% spike)
Z-score of 4.49 indicates highly significant statistical anomaly
Community board repeatedly budgets for 'other request for services for the homeless' and 'programs to de-stigmatize substance misuse,' suggesting chronic unmet need
reporting_angles: Where are the encampments forming? Are there geographic clusters (parks, waterfront, transit hubs)?
Interview outreach workers and CB members: has DHS funding or bed availability changed? Are services adequate?

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Tripled
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 900% increase (z-score: 4.5)—suggesting either organized outdoor gatherings, construction in parks, or a seasonal change in park use patterns.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike)
Z-score of 4.5 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community board has standing request to 'reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park,' suggesting ongoing park infrastructure work
reporting_angles: Which parks are generating complaints? Are there construction projects, events, or hours-of-operation violations?
Is this tied to seasonal foot traffic (spring weather) or specific organized activity?

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints surged to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO against a baseline of 0.6 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.11)—potentially signaling power infrastructure degradation or a localized grid event affecting Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights.
evidence: 5 electrical complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 5.11 indicates statistically significant event
Current data does not show sustained elevation this week, suggesting either resolved incident or underreporting
reporting_angles: Did Con Edison report an outage or infrastructure work in Bay Ridge two weeks ago? Cross-reference with utility records.
Are there building-level failures (old wiring, overloaded circuits) or grid-level issues?
